Looking at this position, I need to identify Black's most forcing move with the White king trapped on h1.

**Position Analysis:**
- White King: h1 (very vulnerable, backed up to the corner)
- White: Queen g4, Rooks a1 & g1, Pawns a2, b2, c2, h4
- Black: King h8, Queen d7, Rooks e3 & f2 (actively placed), Pawns a7, b6, d4, h7

**Key insight:** The f2 rook can deliver check on f1, forcing the king to h2. This initiates a decisive attack.

**Main line:** 1...Rf1+ 2.Kh2 Re1! (threatening both the g1 rook and mate patterns) White collapses—if 3.Rg2 Re2 pins everything; if the rook moves, Qd1 or mate follows shortly.

**Coaching note:**  
Spot trapped kings! White's king on h1 with limited escape squares is completely vulnerable. Your rooks on the 2nd and 3rd ranks dominate. After forcing Kh2 with check, penetrate the back rank (Re1) to finish the attack. When your pieces are active and the enemy king is cornered, look for forcing checks that eliminate escape squares.
